title: Do not let anger set the mouth on fire
summary: The same shabad names anger as the cremation-ground fire that burns through speech. Honor begins when the mouth refuses to become the place where resentment disposes of others.
takeaway: Let anger cool before it uses the mouth as fire.
lifeApplication: If heat is already in your chest, delay the reply long enough to cool it; do not let the mouth become the fire that consumes the person in front of you.

source.shortMeaning: The shabad places slander and anger together: the mouth takes in filth while anger burns like a cremation-ground fire.
source.lifeApplication: When anger heats your reply, wait until the word can leave without burning another person.

evidence.coreClaim: The shabad’s fire image shows that angry speech does not merely express heat; it turns the mouth into a burning place.
evidence.turn: Let the Guru’s warning cool the sentence before anger claims it.
evidence.practicalImplication: If heat is already in your chest, delay the reply long enough to cool it; do not let the mouth become the fire that consumes the person in front of you.
